intro.title: Our Story
intro.subtitle: a scrapbook, 1999 → forever
intro.note: scroll slowly. some photos do things when you tap them 👀

entries.title: A Halloween baby arrives
entries.text: Somewhere, a very dramatic child is born. He will grow up to build websites for a girl he hasn't met yet.

entries.title: The world gets its best idea
entries.text: 350 days later — almost exactly, like the universe was pacing itself — you arrived.

entries.title: October babies 🍂
entries.text: Born 350 days apart, both in October. Same favourite month before we even knew each other. The universe wasn't subtle.

entries.title: We met
entries.text: Two kids in the same school. Nothing special yet. (Everything special, actually. We just didn't know.)

entries.title: The Pollution PPT
entries.text: Our first project together. A PowerPoint about pollution. Tap the film strip — yes, the footage survived.

entries.title: We could NOT stand each other
entries.text: Genuinely. Sworn enemies. If someone had told either of us how this story ends, we'd have laughed them out of the classroom.

entries.title: Fine. Friends.
entries.text: The hating got exhausting. Friendship happened the way it does at that age — suddenly, and like it had always been there.

entries.title: Best friends
entries.text: The upgrade nobody announced but everybody could see.

entries.title: The flirting era
entries.text: “We're just friends.” Sure. Okay. Noted.

entries.title: You said it first
entries.text: You confessed. I'll never let you forget that technically, you liked me first.

entries.title: Back to best friends
entries.text: Wrong time, right person. We filed it away and stayed each other's favourite people.

entries.title: I built you a website
entries.text: A whole website. With a “No” button that ran away from your cursor. You said let's stay friends. The website said nothing. It just stayed online.

archive.label: 🏛️ visit the original — preserved exactly as it was

entries.title: The awkward patch
entries.text: Things got quiet and a little strange for a while. Some chapters are mostly white space.

entries.title: Life rearranged itself
entries.text: Your mom got transferred, and suddenly the kitchen was your problem.

entries.title: The aata lesson 🫓
entries.text: I taught you to knead dough. You were terrible at it. It was the best day I'd had in months. Tap the photo.

entries.title: Almost normal again
entries.text: Slowly, the old rhythm came back. Almost.

entries.title: We lost our way for a while
entries.text: Some seasons are just hard. We stopped talking. I won't pretend it didn't matter — it did. But this scrapbook keeps going, and so did we.

entries.title: A continent of distractions
entries.text: I spent a whole month crossing Europe trying not to think about you. For the record: it did not work. Not in Italy, not in Paris, not anywhere.

entries.title: I just wanted to be there
entries.text: On one of your family's hardest days, nothing else mattered except being near. We talked a little. Small words, after a long silence. It was a start.

entries.title: My sister's roka
entries.text: I invited you. You came. Somewhere between the ceremonies and the chaos, things started feeling like us again.

entries.title: We finally said it
entries.text: I confessed. And this time — you did too. Fourteen years after a pollution PPT, two years after a runaway No button: us. Officially.

egg.text: you found the hidden note. nerd. i love you. — R

entries.title: Long distance, short patience
entries.text: Different cities, same phone glued to hand. Countdowns, call screenshots, tickets booked for any excuse.

finale.text: 15 October 2026. Your birthday. I'm here, in person, no screens between us. And there's a sealed envelope with your name on it.
